name: Andrzej Halicki, Matjaž Nemec - Après le § 10 - Am 112
title: REPORT on the Council position on the draft general budget of the European Union for the financial year 2026
part_text: 10 b. Recalls that the NextGenerationEU (NGEU) instrument, presented as an exceptional recovery plan following the COVID-19 crisis and financed through the issuance of common bonds, was designed in a rushed manner by the Commission, without any thorough impact assessment; recalls, in line with the European Court of Auditors’ Annual Report for the 2024 financial year, that the Commission “has significantly increased its bond issuances over the past five years, having turned to capital markets to finance large-scale programmes such as SURE and NextGenerationEU”; underlines that, according to the same report, “by 2027, the Union’s outstanding borrowings could exceed EUR 900 billion, a figure nearly ten times higher than in 2020, prior to the creation of NextGenerationEU”; warns against the budgetary drift represented by the NGEU instrument, the financing of which will weigh heavily on the Union budget until 2058, due to colossal interest charges that will durably reduce the Union’s financial room for manoeuvre over the next 30 years;
